description: Integrate beads (bd) Dolt-backed task graph into the merger pipeline as a durable checkpoint layer — making merges resumable after crashes/timeouts, giving per-file conflict visibility, and enabling the backend to distinguish transient failures (retry) from genuine blockers (block).

userStories.title: Install beads and Dolt on the host
userStories.description: As a developer, I need bd and dolt available on the host machine so the merger agent can use them when ralph runs.
acceptanceCriteria: dolt binary is installed and dolt --version succeeds in the shell where executor.py runs
bd CLI is installed and bd --version succeeds in the same shell
A scripts/install-deps.sh script documents and automates the installation of both tools
make start still works after installation with no regressions
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: dolt 2.0.1 installed to ~/.local/bin; bd 1.0.4 installed via go install, symlinked to ~/.local/bin. Note: dolt uses 'dolt version' not 'dolt --version'.

userStories.title: Initialize local Dolt remote for the project
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a shared local Dolt remote on the filesystem so all worktrees for the dev-harness project can push and pull beads state to a common location.
acceptanceCriteria: A scripts/init-beads-remote.sh script creates the local Dolt remote at a configurable path (default: <project-root>/.beads-remote/)
The remote path is stored in .env and .env.example as BEADS_REMOTE_PATH
Running the script twice is idempotent (no error on second run)
The .beads-remote/ directory is added to .gitignore
Running bd init && bd dolt remote add origin $BEADS_REMOTE_PATH && bd dolt push from a test worktree succeeds without error
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: BEADS_REMOTE_PATH stored as file:// URL. Script uses dolt init to create the remote. CGO build of bd required for embedded Dolt mode (updated install-deps.sh). Idempotent: checks for .dolt directory before re-running dolt init.

userStories.title: Define the merge molecule template
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a beads molecule template that represents the phases of a merge job so the merger agent can spawn it at the start of each merge.
acceptanceCriteria: A molecule file exists at backend/beads/merge-molecule.yml (or the correct format beads supports — check bd molecule --help)
Molecule defines five top-level phase beads with explicit dependencies: fetch-main -> rebase -> run-tests -> merge-push -> cleanup
Molecule includes metadata field execution_agent_type: merger
bd molecule spawn (or equivalent command) produces the expected bead graph in a test worktree
bd list --json output contains the five phase beads with correct dependency edges after spawning
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Formula at .beads/formulas/merge-molecule.formula.toml (TOML, not YAML). Uses bd mol pour to spawn. bd list --json returns flat list with dependencies array (type: blocks for sequential deps). Five steps: fetch-main -> rebase -> run-tests -> merge-push -> cleanup. execution_agent_type stored under [metadata] table.

userStories.title: Update merger.md — beads initialization and phase loop
userStories.description: As the merger agent, I need to initialize beads at the start of a merge and work through phase beads using bd ready, so my progress is checkpointed after every phase.
acceptanceCriteria: merger.md instructs the agent to run bd init and bd dolt remote add origin $BEADS_REMOTE_PATH at the start if no .beads/ directory exists in the worktree
If .beads/ already exists, the agent runs bd dolt pull to restore prior progress before calling bd ready
Agent spawns the merge molecule if bd list --json returns no beads; otherwise skips molecule creation
For each phase bead returned by bd ready --json --limit 1, the agent performs the corresponding git work, then calls bd close <id> and bd dolt push before moving to the next bead
The <promise>COMPLETE</promise> signal is only written after the cleanup bead is closed
A fresh merge (no prior beads) completes end-to-end and the ticket reaches done state
A simulated resume (manually pre-close the fetch-main bead, then run merger) skips fetch and begins at rebase
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: merger.md restructured with: beads init section (bd init + bd dolt remote add origin $BEADS_REMOTE_PATH for fresh start; bd dolt pull for resume), molecule spawn guarded by bd list --json empty check, phase loop using bd ready --json --limit 1 → bd close <id> → bd dolt push for each of fetch-main/rebase/run-tests/merge-push/cleanup, COMPLETE signal only after cleanup bead closed.

userStories.title: Create and clean up per-file conflict sub-beads
userStories.description: As the merger agent, I need to create one child bead per conflicting file during rebase so each file's resolution is tracked individually, then clean up beads state after a successful merge.
acceptanceCriteria: After git rebase origin/main reports conflicts, the agent runs git status --short to identify all conflicted files
For each conflicted file, the agent creates a child bead under the rebase bead: bd create resolve-conflict:<filename> --parent <rebase-bead-id>
The agent resolves each file, then calls bd close <conflict-bead-id> and bd dolt push per file before continuing rebase
The run-tests bead only becomes ready (returned by bd ready) after all conflict sub-beads are closed
After the cleanup bead is closed, the agent calls bd dolt push then removes the .beads/ directory from the worktree with rm -rf .beads/
If no conflicts occur during rebase, no conflict sub-beads are created
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Replace merge-failures.json with beads state in the backend
userStories.description: As the backend, I need to read beads state to determine merge outcome — distinguishing transient failures from genuine blockers — instead of relying on merge-failures.json.
acceptanceCriteria: merger.md no longer instructs the agent to write merge-failures.json; genuine blockers are instead recorded as bead metadata: bd update <id> --metadata '{"blocker": true, "category": "...", "detail": "..."}'

backend/app/agent_loop.py has a _read_beads_state(worktree_path: str) -> dict | None function that runs bd list --json in the worktree as a subprocess and returns parsed output, or None if .beads/ does not exist
In try_pickup_and_run(), after ralph exits for the merger case, the code reads beads state instead of merge-failures.json
Exit 0 + no open beads -> complete_ticket()
Exit non-zero + open beads with no blocker metadata -> re-dispatch merger via _schedule_pickup('merger') (transient failure, do not block)
Any exit + at least one bead with blocker: true in metadata -> fail_ticket() -> ticket goes to blocked
The stale merge-failures.json cleanup block in agent_loop.py lines 104-118 is removed for the merger case
Unit tests cover all three outcome branches using a mocked bd list response
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Merger resumability in the timeout handler
userStories.description: As the backend, when the merger agent times out, I need to check whether beads has partial progress and retry rather than always returning the ticket to a manual state.
acceptanceCriteria: A merger_resume_count integer column (default 0) is added to the Ticket model in backend/app/models.py and a corresponding DB migration is added to _migrate_schema() in database.py
In backend/app/routers/agents.py, the merger timeout handler reads beads state from the worktree after a timeout using _read_beads_state()

If beads shows partial progress (at least one bead closed, at least one open, none with blocker: true) AND merger_resume_count < 3: increment merger_resume_count, call _schedule_pickup('merger'), and leave the ticket in in_merge state
If beads shows no progress (all beads open) or a genuine blocker bead: run the existing timeout logic (ticket returns to to_do or blocked)
If .beads/ does not exist in the worktree: fall back to the existing <promise>COMPLETE</promise> log-check behavior unchanged
If merger_resume_count reaches 3: stop retrying, call fail_ticket() with a note describing how many resume attempts were made and which bead it was stuck on
Unit tests cover: partial-progress retry, no-progress fallback, blocker fallback, and resume-count cap (3 -> block)
Typecheck passes
